mainTopic: The impurity of נבלת עוף טהור according to רבי מאיר, counting ראשון and שני, and the three camps for the burned bulls and goats
overview: The amud opens by finishing a point from the previous page: according to רבי מאיר, a כזית of נבלת עוף טהור is enough to make food impure. Not yet having reached the throat does not count as a missing action. A משנה in טהרות that requires a כביצה is brought as a challenge. The גמרא answers that this rule follows the רבנן, even though the first and last parts of that משנה follow רבי מאיר. Next, רבי זירא gives one rule for counting levels of impurity: we count ראשון and שני only from something that can make a person impure. This rule settles two questions, one about נבלת עוף טהור and one about foods joined by liquid. The גמרא then returns to the משנה about the burned bulls and goats. A ברייתא shows that the carriers' clothes become impure once the offering leaves one camp, while the burning itself happens outside three camps, which it proves from extra words in the verses. Finally, the גמרא explains that רבי שמעון uses 'outside the camp' for רבי אליעזר's גזירה שוה linking these offerings to the פרה אדומה. That comparison continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Not yet reaching the throat does not count as a missing action
steps.stepSummary: The reasoning ends with a rule: the bird carcass not yet having reached the throat does not count as a missing action. So, in this view, a כזית is enough to make food impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Lacking only being brought close (to the throat) is not treated like lacking an action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why, in this view, a כזית of a kosher bird's carcass is enough to make food impure. Not having reached the throat yet is not a real 'missing action.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נבלת עוף טהור causes its strong impurity only once it is in the throat. One could argue that until then it is 'missing something,' so it should need the usual food amount of a כביצה. This line says no: the only thing missing is bringing it close, and that is not counted as a missing action, so the smaller amount of a כזית still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: lacking only being brought close (here, to the throat)
lacking an action; something that still needs a real act before it gets its status
the carcass of a kosher bird that was not properly slaughtered
an olive-size amount

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'brought close' with an act a person must do to the food. The point is that this missing step is NOT treated as a real missing action.

phrases.english: Lacking only being brought close
phrases.notes: He means the bird's meat has not yet reached the throat, where its strong impurity takes effect.

phrases.english: is not considered like lacking an action.

steps.triggerLanguage: מחוסר קריבה לאו כמחוסר מעשה דמי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reasoning from the previous page for why a כזית is enough according to רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lacking only 'being brought close' is not counted as lacking an action, so a כזית of נבלת עוף טהור makes food impure.

steps.title: A משנה says an egg-size is needed
steps.stepSummary: An objection from a משנה in טהרות: a נבלת עוף טהור makes food impure only with a כביצה. Isn't that משנה following רבי מאיר?
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected: Thirteen things were said about the carcass of a kosher bird, and this is one of them: it needs intention, it does not need to be made susceptible, and it makes food impure with an egg-size. Isn't this רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone challenges the previous claim using a משנה. That משנה says a נבלת עוף טהור makes food impure only with a כביצה, not a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step said that according to רבי מאיר a כזית is enough. The objection assumes this משנה is רבי מאיר's view, because its other details match him. If so, רבי מאיר requires a כביצה, which contradicts the claim.

keyTerms.meaning: intention; a person deciding to treat it as food
being made able to become impure, through contact with liquid
the impurity of food
an egg-size amount

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him: Thirteen things were said
phrases.notes: The objection comes from a משנה, טהרות 1:1.

phrases.english: about the carcass of a kosher bird,
and this is one of them:
it needs intention (to be eaten),
and it does not need to be made susceptible (by liquid),
and it makes food impure with an egg-size.
What, is it not רבי מאיר?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim from step 1 that, for רבי מאיר, a כזית is enough.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי מאיר holds a כזית of נבלת עוף טהור makes food impure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה that seems to follow רבי מאיר requires a כביצה, which contradicts the claim.

steps.title: The משנה follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: Answer: the משנה is not רבי מאיר; it follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection by saying the משנה follows the רבנן, not רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כביצה ruling belongs to the רבנן, then it says nothing about what רבי מאיר holds. So רבי מאיר can still say a כזית is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: the Sages; the majority opinion that disagrees with an individual

phrases.english: No, it is the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the source to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is רבי מאיר, so he requires a כביצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is the רבנן, so רבי מאיר can still hold a כזית is enough.

steps.title: The first part of the משנה matches רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: Challenge to the answer: the first part of the משנה (needs intention, no need to be made susceptible) is known as רבי מאיר's view. So the end of it should be רבי מאיר too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the first part teaches: it needs intention and does not need to be made susceptible. Whom do we know holds this view? רבי מאיר. And since the first part is רבי מאיר, the last part is also רבי מאיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. The first part of the same משנה follows רבי מאיר, so it is hard to say the end follows the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea of 'needs intention but no need to be made susceptible' is known from רבי מאיר, as taught earlier. Normally one משנה follows one view from start to end. So the כביצה rule at the end should also be רבי מאיר, and the problem comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: the first part of a teaching
the last part of a teaching
a line of reasoning or view

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. The גמרא is attacking the answer in step 3 and bringing back the question from step 2.
steps.whyThisMatters: It uses a common tool: a single משנה is assumed to follow one opinion all the way through, unless there is a reason to split it.

phrases.english: But the first part teaches:
it needs intention and does not need to be made susceptible;

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ הַאי סְבָרָא – רַבִּי מֵאִיר;
phrases.english: and whom have you heard holds this view? רבי מאיר;
and since the first part is רבי מאיר,
the last part is also רבי מאיר!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 3 by showing the first part of the משנה is רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה follows the רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first part of the משנה matches רבי מאיר's known view, so the end, which says כביצה, should be his too. That brings back the contradiction.

steps.title: Each part of the משנה can follow its own view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the first part of the משנה can follow רבי מאיר while the next part follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are these two parts really tied together? This part is as it is, and that part is as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge from step 4. It says the two parts of the משנה do not have to follow the same תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that since the first part is רבי מאיר, the rest must be too. The גמרא answers that a משנה can hold different views in different parts. So the כביצה rule can still be the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really connected? A way of saying two things don't depend on each other
This one is as it is, and that one is as it is. Each stands on its own

phrases.english: Are these really connected?!
This one is as it is, and that one is as it is.
phrases.notes: He means the first part can be רבי מאיר and the middle part can be the רבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4 by separating the parts of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the משנה between different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the first part is רבי מאיר, the whole משנה must be רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each part of a משנה can follow a different view, so the middle can be the רבנן.

steps.title: The last part of the משנה is also רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the last part of the משנה also follows רבי מאיר, so would the משנה really switch to the רבנן only in the middle?
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at the last part of the משנה: the שחיטה or מליקה of the bird saves it from the impurity of a נבלה, even if it turns out to be a טריפה. Who holds this idea? רבי מאיר. So the first and last parts are רבי מאיר and only the middle part is the רבנן?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a stronger challenge. The ending of the same משנה also follows רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Switching views once might be acceptable. But if both the start and the end are רבי מאיר, it seems odd for the middle alone to be the רבנן. This makes it harder to say the כביצה rule is not רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering with a knife
Pinching the back of a bird's neck, the way a bird קרבן is killed
An animal or bird with a fatal defect
The middle part

phrases.english: But from the fact that the last part teaches:
its slaughtering and its pinching
keep it pure from its impurity even when it is a טריפה;
phrases.notes: Because it was slaughtered or pinched, it does not get the impurity of a נבלה, even though it is a טריפה.

phrases.english: whom have you heard holding this reasoning?
Rabbi Meir.
So the first part and the last part are Rabbi Meir,
and the middle part is the Rabbis?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 5 by showing the end of the משנה is also רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the middle part of the משנה, the כביצה rule, follows the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both the start and the end follow רבי מאיר, it is unlikely that the middle alone switches to the רבנן.

steps.title: Yes, the middle part alone follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the split: the first and last parts are רבי מאיר, and the middle is the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. The first and last parts are רבי מאיר, and the middle part is the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא simply says yes. The משנה really is split this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though it seems strange, the גמרא accepts that the middle part follows a different view. So the כביצה rule is the רבנן. This leaves room for the rule from step 1 that, for רבי מאיר, a כזית is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה in טהרות is split. The first and last parts follow רבי מאיר, and the middle part, which says a כביצה is needed, follows the רבנן. So according to רבי מאיר, a כזית of נבלת עוף טהור can still make food impure.

phrases.english: Yes;
the first part and the last part are Rabbi Meir,
and the middle part is the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the point raised in step 6 and stands by the split.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A משנה would not switch views only in its middle part.
steps.terutzMaskana: It does switch. The middle part is the רבנן, so it is no proof about רבי מאיר.

steps.title: Does a נבלת עוף טהור count levels of impurity for רבי מאיר?
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא asks רבי זירא whether, according to רבי מאיר, food touched by a נבלת עוף טהור becomes a ראשון and then makes a שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said to רבי זירא: Don't sit down until you tell me this: according to רבי מאיר, does a נבלת עוף טהור make food a ראשון, which then makes other food a שני? Or do we not count ראשון and שני this way?
steps.whatsHappening: A new discussion begins. רב המנונא asks how strong the impurity of a נבלת עוף טהור is according to רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an אב הטומאה makes food a ראשון, and that food makes other food a שני. Since for רבי מאיר this bird makes food impure even without the usual preparation, the question is whether it acts like an אב הטומאה. If not, maybe it acts only like a ראשון, and the food it touches becomes just a שני.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't sit down. Literally, don't sit on your legs. A way of asking for an answer right away
The carcass of a kosher bird that died without proper שחיטה
We count, here meaning counting levels of impurity
First and second levels of impurity

steps.confusionAlert: This is a brand-new question, not part of the argument about the split משנה. It asks about the level of impurity, not the amount (כזית or כביצה).

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הַמְנוּנָא לְרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said to Rabbi Zeira:
Do not sit down,
phrases.notes: Literally, "don't sit on your legs." He wants the answer right now.

phrases.english: until you tell me this matter:
the carcass of a kosher bird,
according to Rabbi Meir,
do we count a first and a second level from it,
or do we not count a first and a second level?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הַמְנוּנָא לְרַבִּי זֵירָא: לָא תִּיתֵּיב אַכַּרְעָךְ עַד דְּאָמְרַתְּ לִי הָא מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about רבי מאיר's view of נבלת עוף טהור, now about levels of impurity.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, for רבי מאיר, a נבלת עוף טהור acts like an אב הטומאה, making food a ראשון that then makes a שני, or only like a ראשון.

steps.title: Only something that makes a person impure starts the count
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers רב המנונא: something that makes a person impure by touch starts a count of ראשון and שני. Something that does not, such as נבלת עוף טהור, does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Anything that makes a person impure by touching him starts the count of first and second levels. Anything that does not make a person impure by touching him does not start that count.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the question from step 8 with a general rule. נבלת עוף טהור does not make a person impure by touch, so we do not count a ראשון and a שני from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב המנונא asked whether food touched by נבלת עוף טהור becomes a ראשון that can then make a שני. Real sources of טומאה make a person impure by touch, but נבלת עוף טהור only makes impure when it is swallowed. So it does not act as a source that begins the count. It is treated more like impure food itself.

keyTerms.meaning: we count from it (start counting levels of טומאה)
first level of טומאה
second level of טומאה
by touching

steps.whyThisMatters: This one rule becomes the measuring stick for the next question in the sugya too.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבי זירא answering רב המנונא's question from the step before.

phrases.english: Wherever it makes a person impure by touch –
we count from it a first and a second,
phrases.notes: He means the food it touches becomes a ראשון, and that food can then make a שני.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּאֵין מְטַמֵּא אָדָם בְּמַגָּע –
phrases.english: wherever it does not make a person impure by touch –
we do not count from it a first and a second.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כֹּל הֵיכָא דִּמְטַמֵּא אָדָם בְּמַגָּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question רב המנונא asked in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: We only count ראשון and שני from something that makes a person impure by touch. נבלת עוף טהור does not, so we do not count from it.

steps.title: Foods joined by liquid: do we count first and second?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks about the משנה that says foods joined by liquid combine for light טומאה but not for heavy טומאה. Do we count ראשון and שני from them?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked רבי אמי בר חייא (some say he asked רבי אבין בר כהנא): We learned in a משנה that foods joined together by liquid count as joined for the light kind of טומאה, but not for the heavy kind. Do we count first and second levels from them, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבי זירא is the one asking. He brings a משנה about foods joined by liquid and asks whether they start a count of ראשון and שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pieces are joined well enough to pass on light טומאה, the kind that reaches food. They are not joined well enough to pass on heavy טומאה, the kind that reaches a person. The question is whether this limited joining makes them a full source that starts the count of ראשון and שני.

keyTerms.meaning: connections between foods
light טומאה (the kind that reaches foods)
heavy טומאה (the kind that reaches a person)

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא מֵרַבִּי אַמֵּי בַּר חִיָּיא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira asked Rabbi Ami bar Chiya,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ מֵרַבִּי אָבִין בַּר כָּהֲנָא,
phrases.english: and some say he asked Rabbi Avin bar Kahana,
about what we learned in a Mishnah:
Foods connected to each other through liquid –
count as a connection for the light impurity,
but are not a connection for the heavy impurity;
do we count from it a first and a second,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵין מוֹנִין בּוֹ רִאשׁוֹן וְשֵׁנִי?
phrases.english: or do we not count from it a first and a second?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא מֵרַבִּי אַמֵּי בַּר חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new, related question about counting ראשון and שני, this time for foods joined by liquid.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do foods joined by liquid, which combine only for light טומאה, start a count of ראשון and שני?

steps.title: Same rule: no impurity to a person means no count
steps.stepSummary: The answer uses the same rule as before. Since the joined foods cannot make a person impure, we do not count ראשון and שני from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Anything that makes a person impure starts the count of first and second levels. Anything that does not make a person impure does not start the count.
steps.whatsHappening: The rabbi who was asked answers with the same rule used in step 9. The joined pieces do not combine to make a person impure, so we do not count ראשון and שני from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the joining by liquid does not work for heavy טומאה, so these pieces cannot make a person impure. Under the rule, only something that makes a person impure starts the count. So the joined pieces are treated like ordinary impure food, not like a source.

keyTerms.meaning: wherever, in any case where
that makes a person impure

steps.whatToRemember: One rule answers both questions: we count ראשון and שני only from something that can make a person impure. נבלת עוף טהור and foods joined by liquid both fail this test.
steps.confusionAlert: This rule is not new. It is the same rule from step 9, now applied to a different case, the foods joined by liquid.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Wherever it makes a person impure –
we count from it a first and a second,
where it does not make a person impure –
we do not count from it a first and a second.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כֹּל הֵיכָא דִּמְטַמֵּא אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's question from step 10 using the rule from step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Foods joined by liquid cannot make a person impure, so we do not count ראשון and שני from them.

steps.title: Asking for the source of the rule that the carriers' clothes become impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'these and those went out' and asks where this rule comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Once these and those went out (their clothes became impure).' From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and asks for its source in the Torah. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that the כהנים carrying the burned bulls and goats make their clothes impure once they leave. The question is exactly where this begins and what verse teaches it.

keyTerms.meaning: These and those went out: the words quoted from the משנה
From where are these matters? The standard way to ask for a source
Impurity of clothes: the clothes of the person carrying the offering become טמא

phrases.english: These and those went out.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה about the carriers of the burned bulls and goats. Once they went out, their clothes became impure.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. It moves from the counting of ראשון and שני back to the משנה's rule about carrying the burned offerings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for the rule that the carriers' clothes become impure once they go out.

steps.title: Clothes become impure once the offering leaves just one camp
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא contrasts two verses. Elsewhere the Torah requires three camps, but here it mentions only one. This teaches that the clothes become impure after one camp.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Elsewhere the Torah speaks of outside three camps. Here it speaks of one camp. This tells you that once the offering goes out beyond one camp, it makes the carrier's clothes impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. Clothes become impure as soon as the offering passes the first camp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The burning itself takes place outside all three camps. The verse about יום כיפור mentions only one camp. That difference tells us the clothes become impure at the earlier point, after the first camp.

keyTerms.meaning: Three camps: the camp of the משכן, the camp of the לויים, and the camp of ישראל
One camp: the first camp, of the משכן
Makes clothes impure

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up two different places. The offering is burned outside three camps, but the carrier's clothes already become impure once it passes the first camp.

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: לְהַלָּן הוּא אוֹמֵר – חוּץ לְשָׁלֹשׁ מַחֲנוֹת,
phrases.english: There it says: outside three camps,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the other verses about these bulls. The גמרא shows how they teach three camps in the next steps.

phrases.english: here: to one camp;
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:27, about the יום כיפור bull and goat.

phrases.english: to tell you:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּצָא חוּץ לְמַחֲנֶה אַחַת – מְטַמֵּא בְּגָדִים.
phrases.english: once it has gone out beyond one camp, it makes clothes impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question from step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The contrast between 'three camps' elsewhere and 'one camp' here shows that the clothes become impure after the first camp.

steps.title: How do we know about three camps in the first place?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the assumption that the burning happens outside three camps.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that rule itself, from where do we learn it?
steps.whatsHappening: The answer in step 13 assumed that the burning is outside three camps. Now the גמרא asks where that comes from. This sets up a second ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 13 depends on the contrast 'three camps there, one camp here.' So the גמרא must show that the 'three camps' part really has a source.

keyTerms.meaning: And that itself, from where do we know it? Asks for the source of something just assumed

phrases.english: And that itself, from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the assumption used in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the bulls and goats are burned outside three camps.

steps.title: The ברייתא states the three-camp rule and asks whether it might be only one
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'outside the camp' about the כהן גדול's bull as outside three camps. It then asks whether it could mean only one camp.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'He shall take the whole bull outside the camp' means outside three camps. Do you say three camps, or is it only one camp?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא states its claim of three camps. Then it asks the obvious doubt: maybe the verse means just one camp. This sets up the proof that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in ויקרא 4:12 says only 'outside the camp,' which on its own sounds like one camp. The ברייתא admits this and will answer it using extra words found in other verses.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall take out the whole bull: the verse about the כהן גדול's חטאת
You say this, or is it only that? A ברייתא formula that raises a doubt before proving its point

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"And he shall carry out the whole bull
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:12, about the bull of the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: outside the camp" —
outside three camps.
You say outside three camps;
or is it only one camp?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר חוּץ לְשָׁלֹשׁ מַחֲנוֹת; אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מַחֲנֶה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the ברייתא that answers step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bull is taken outside three camps. The ברייתא raises the doubt that it might be only one.

steps.title: Extra words about the community bull add a second camp
steps.stepSummary: The verse about פר העדה says 'outside the camp' even though it was not needed. So it teaches a second camp.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the Torah says 'outside the camp' about the community's bull, it did not need to. It already said 'as he burned the first bull.' So the extra words give it a second camp.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves the second camp from words in the Torah that seem extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'as he burned the first bull' already copies every rule of the כהן גדול's bull, including 'outside the camp.' Saying 'outside the camp' again is extra, so it adds one more camp beyond the first.

keyTerms.meaning: The community's bull: a חטאת brought for a mistake made by the whole community
There is no need to say it: points out that the words seem extra
Second camp: the camp of the לויים

phrases.english: When it says regarding the community's bull:
"outside the camp" —
which there is no need to say,
since it is already stated:
"as he burned the first bull";
phrases.notes: The 'first bull' is the כהן גדול's bull from earlier in the פרק. Its rules already include 'outside the camp.'

phrases.english: to give it a second camp.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the ברייתא's doubt from step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That the burning must be beyond a second camp.

steps.title: Extra words about the ashes add a third camp
steps.stepSummary: The verse about the ashes says 'outside the camp' even though it was not needed. So it teaches a third camp, which completes the three.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the Torah says 'outside the camp' about the ashes, it did not need to. It already said 'on the ash-heap it shall be burned.' So the extra words give it a third camp.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves the third camp the same way, from more words that seem extra. This finishes the proof of three camps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know the bull is burned at the ash-heap, so the ashes' place outside the camp is known. Saying 'outside the camp' again about the ashes is extra, so it adds a third camp.

keyTerms.meaning: Ashes from the מזבח
The place where the ashes are poured out
Third camp: the camp of ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: There are three camps in all: the first from the basic verse, a second from the extra words about פר העדה, and a third from the extra words about the ashes. The burning is outside all three, but the carrier's clothes become impure once the offering passes the first camp.

phrases.english: When it says "outside the camp" regarding the ashes —
which there is no need to say,
since it is already stated:
"on the place where the ashes are poured out it shall be burned";
to give it a third camp.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the same pattern as step 16 to add the third camp and finish the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That the burning must be beyond a third camp.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the source for the three-camp rule. Step 13's proof that clothes become impure after one camp depended on it.

steps.title: What does רבי שמעון do with 'outside the camp'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי שמעון learns from the words 'outside the camp', since he does not use them for the rule about clothes becoming impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון, what does he do with this phrase 'outside the camp'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי שמעון. He does not learn the clothes rule from 'outside the camp', so the גמרא asks what those words teach him instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 13, the words 'outside the camp' taught that the carrier's clothes become impure once the offering leaves one camp. רבי שמעון holds that the clothes become impure only once the burning has started, so for him those words seem to have no job. The Torah does not waste words, so the גמרא asks what he uses them for.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? In other words, what does he learn from this verse?
Outside the camp

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon,
this phrase 'outside the camp',
what does he do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the verse used in Step 13 and asks how רבי שמעון, who disagrees with that teaching, explains it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי שמעון learns from the words 'outside the camp' in the verse about the יום כיפור offerings.

steps.title: A גזירה שוה teaches three camps
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון uses the phrase for רבי אליעזר's גזירה שוה. Because 'outside the camp' appears in both cases, both cases are burned outside three camps.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says, it says here 'outside the camp' and it says there 'outside the camp'. Just as there it means outside three camps, so too here it means outside three camps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון uses 'outside the camp' to link two cases that share the same words. Through that link, the rule of burning outside three camps passes from one case to the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words, 'outside the camp', appear about the יום כיפור bull and goat and about the פרה אדומה. A גזירה שוה treats matching words as a link, so a rule in one case applies to the other. Here the three-camp rule of the burned bulls is passed to the פרה אדומה. This gives the phrase a real job for רבי שמעון, so it is not a wasted word.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
It says here... and it says there. This is the opening formula of a גזירה שוה.

steps.confusionAlert: The link works in both directions. The three-camp rule passes from the burned bulls to the פרה אדומה, and in the next step the 'east of ירושלים' rule passes from the פרה to the bulls.

phrases.english: He needs it for that which is taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
It is stated here: 'Outside the camp,'
and it is stated there: 'Outside the camp';
phrases.notes: The other case is the פרה אדומה, במדבר 19:3. The three-camp rule, proven above for the burned bulls, carries over to it.

phrases.english: just as there, it means outside three camps,
so too here, it means outside three camps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18 by giving the phrase a different job: a גזירה שוה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון uses 'outside the camp' for רבי אליעזר's גזירה שוה. It links the יום כיפור offerings and the פרה אדומה, so both are burned outside three camps.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבי שמעון does not ignore the words. He uses them for a different teaching, so his view about the clothes still holds up.

steps.title: Second comparison begins: east of ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא starts a second comparison: just as there the burning is east of ירושלים. The sentence finishes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And just as there it is east of ירושלים...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא begins a second rule to pass along through the same link: the place of burning is east of ירושלים. This step only sets up that comparison, and the next amud finishes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same shared words now carry a second rule, which is about direction rather than distance. The פרה אדומה must be burned facing the front of the אהל מועד, so it is burned to the east. The ברייתא is getting ready to apply this direction to the other case as well.

keyTerms.meaning: To its east
ירושלים, the city of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: And just as there,
phrases.notes: Here 'there' is the פרה אדומה, which must be burned facing the front of the אהל מועד (במדבר 19:4).

phrases.english: it is east of Jerusalem,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same גזירה שוה from Step 19 to begin passing along a second rule, about direction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Through the same link, the פרה אדומה's burning east of ירושלים is about to be applied to the other case. The sentence continues on the next amud.
